doc.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe. Utica, New York, November 6, 2010 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Why young people had more time before computers; hiding behind music
summary: Compares distractions today with her own childhood, and says music was an escape from a religious home.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Why is it that — I mean this is not really a musical question so much, but you are taking about young people had more time pre-computers. What is that about?

Well I don’t know, it just seems like there’s a lot more distractions now. Meaning that we didn’t have the Facebook, we didn’t have email. I don’t know. It’s hard to say. That’s a hard question because certain kids are more disciplined that others. And I mean really, these days, if you’re going to get work done and really trying to succeed with something, you’ve got to limit your time on Facebook, you’ve got to limit your time on email. You know what I mean? Whereas back then there was not that and we weren’t allowed to watch too much TV and I wasn’t as interested in TV as I was trying to work on a Schumann piano piece.

So I don’t know. For me it’s just I hid behind music a bit too. I grew up in a religious house and all of that didn’t really appeal to me too much so music was a little way out for me. I notice this with kids that I teach now. Their time is so, you know, I mean chopped up with, it seems like there’s more pressure on kids too, academically, because we’re in different economic times. You know what I mean? There’s more pressure on kids these days.
